title: 9 to 5
label: Island
format: CD single (two editions) and 12-inch, per Wikipedia

type.basis: Evidence specimen at the pop edge of the scene: one 2006 review calls it peppy pop and contrasts it with her earlier, scatter-mouthed grime.

sound.text: Contains a sample from the film Time Bandits (Wikipedia).
PopMatters (2006) places it at the poppy end of her range, calling it 'peppy pop'.
The FADER (2005) says her sing-song choruses temper the roughness associated with grime, and that her album draws on ska, electro and new wave.

context.text: Official Singles Chart peak no. 33 (first chart date 20/08/2005, 3 weeks); no. 17 on the Official Dance Singles Chart (OCC).
A re-recorded Ordinary Boys version, 'Nine2Five' (2006), reached UK no. 6 (Wikipedia); The FADER (2005) reported the Ordinary Boys had been commissioned to cover it.
NPR (2007) introduces her as coming out of Britain's grime scene.

calls.label: peppy pop (the track); grime-pop (her earlier work)
'alternative grime' with ska and punk influences (the then-forthcoming album)

rels.other: The Ordinary Boys vs. Lady Sovereign - Nine2Five (2006)

uncertainty: OCC catalogue 12IS898 presumably the 12-inch; CD catalogue numbers not found. Wikipedia's Def Jam/Island attribution not checked against a sleeve. No source opened calls the single itself grime; genre calls are about the artist or album.
tracklist: CD1: 9 to 5 / Tango. CD2: original, 'Nine2Five' (Ordinary Boys remix), JME remix, two Tony Senghore mixes, video. 12-inch: five tracks including original, JME remix and two Tony Senghore mixes (Wikipedia). Writers: Louise Harman and Gabriel Olegavich. Later on the album Public Warning (2006).

audit.note: Single not listed; artist page links '9 To 5' to a Public Warning album id 1444047621 (different from the album id 1445866050 shown here). Album page shows 'Hip-Hop/Rap · 2006', ℗ 2006 Universal Island Records. Also 'Nine2Five (feat. Lady Sovereign)' by The Ordinary Boys (2006).
Single not in the Lady Sovereign discography (5 releases, all Hip-Hop/Rap). Public Warning is listed twice (Universal-Island Records Ltd., Hip-Hop/Rap) but its track list was not checked.
